title: Transitioning to Post-Quantum Cryptography (joint statement)
summary: Joint statement hosted and co-signed by BSI on transitioning to post-quantum cryptography, noting that several well-studied PQC alternatives to currently deployed vulnerable cryptography are available.

title: Transition deadlines agreed for post-quantum cryptography in classified IT (VS-IT)
summary: BSI announcement that deadlines have been agreed for migrating German classified IT systems (VS-IT) to post-quantum cryptography.

title: Cooperation group publishes EU roadmap for quantum-safe cryptography (press release)
summary: BSI press release on the publication of an EU roadmap for quantum-safe cryptography, prepared by a working group on post-quantum cryptography established in 2024.

title: BSI and partners from 17 other EU member states demand transition to post-quantum cryptography
summary: BSI press release announcing that BSI and partner agencies from 17 other EU member states jointly call for the transition to post-quantum cryptography.

title: Post-quantum cryptography (topic page)
summary: BSI information page explaining post-quantum cryptography as cryptographic schemes assumed to remain unbreakable even with the help of a quantum computer.

title: Quantum technologies and quantum-safe cryptography (topic page)
summary: BSI topic page on quantum technologies and quantum-safe cryptography, referencing the BSI guideline 'Quantum-safe cryptography - fundamentals, current developments and recommendations'.

title: Position paper on quantum key distribution
summary: Position paper on quantum key distribution published by BSI under its quantum technologies and quantum-safe cryptography workstream.

title: BSI TR-02102-1 Cryptographic mechanisms: recommendations and key lengths
summary: Technical Guideline in which BSI provides an assessment of cryptographic mechanisms and key lengths; recent updates extend the recommendations to post-quantum cryptography.

title: Government plans roadmap for post-quantum cryptography
summary: Bundestag news item reporting that the Federal Government plans a roadmap for post-quantum cryptography and supports implementation through the funding directive 'Bringing post-quantum cryptography into applications'.

title: Bundestag printed paper 21/2526 on the transition to quantum-safe cryptography
summary: Bundestag printed paper stating that a national project plan for the transition to quantum-safe cryptography is currently being drawn up in line with the relevant recommendation.

title: Bundestag printed paper 20/8104 on post-quantum cryptography readiness
summary: Bundestag printed paper stating that Germany is well positioned on post-quantum cryptography and that the BSI issued early recommendations for the migration to PQC.

title: Bundesrat session 1065 explanatory note on PQC migration in national cybersecurity strategies
summary: Explanatory note for the Bundesrat's 1065th session concerning an obligation for member states to adopt concepts for the migration to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) within their national cybersecurity strategies.

title: Bundesrat printed paper 166/24 on post-quantum cryptography
summary: Bundesrat printed paper describing post-quantum cryptography (PQC) as a promising approach and referencing the BSI's recommendations for action on post-quantum cryptography.

title: Looking ahead: how will quantum computing change banking? (speech)
summary: Bundesbank speech on quantum computing in banking, noting the Federal Government's goal of initiating the migration to post-quantum cryptography in security-critical areas by 2026.

title: Bringing post-quantum cryptography into applications (funding call)
summary: BMBF funding announcement for projects on the development and analysis of cryptographic schemes that withstand quantum computers, aimed at bringing post-quantum cryptography into application.

title: Federal Government action plan for quantum technologies (Handlungskonzept)
summary: Federal Government action plan for quantum technologies, which addresses post-quantum cryptography as an important element in the quantum technology context, noting it is implemented on classical hardware.

title: Agenda for cybersecurity research
summary: BMBF cybersecurity research agenda that includes researching post-quantum cryptography and bringing it into broad application to be prepared for the future era of quantum computers.

title: Research programme quantum systems
summary: BMBF federal research programme on quantum systems that covers post-quantum cryptography (PQK) among the topics addressed in the programme.

title: Digital. Secure. Sovereign. (IT security research framework programme)
summary: Federal research framework programme for IT security noting that diverging international developments are expected for new algorithms such as post-quantum cryptography.

title: Federal Report on Research and Innovation 2020
summary: Federal Government report on research and innovation referencing post-quantum cryptography, whose aim is to develop encryption schemes that remain secure in the era of quantum computers.

title: Quantum-secure communication (guideline)
summary: Guideline by the German digital industry association Bitkom on quantum-secure communication, addressing quantum-safe cryptography methods designed to withstand the capabilities of quantum computers. Industry association rather than a government body, flagged for review.

title: PQC update from BSI: policies, activities and roadmap (presentation)
summary: BSI conference presentation outlining the agency's PQC policies, activities and roadmap, including continued migration to post-quantum cryptography for high-security applications. Hosted on a conference platform rather than an official BSI domain, flagged for review.

title: BSI TR-02102-2 Cryptographic mechanisms: recommendations on TLS
summary: BSI Technical Guideline with recommendations for the use of the Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol, part of the TR-02102 series of cryptographic recommendations. Explicit PQC reference not visible in the candidate snippet, flagged for review.

title: Federal Quantum Alliance (Bundesquantenallianz) resources
summary: Resource page of the Bundesquantenallianz, a cooperation of federally owned companies preparing for the age of quantum computing. Explicit PQC reference not visible in the candidate snippet, flagged for review.

title: Bundestag printed paper on the PQC roadmap (DIP full text)
summary: Machine-readable full text of a Bundestag printed paper discussing the presentation of a roadmap for post-quantum cryptography in Germany and the promotion of migration to quantum-safe cryptography. May duplicate one of the included Drucksachen, flagged for review.

title: BSI empfiehlt Ende klassischer asymmetrischer Verschlüsselungsverfahren
summary: BSI press release (11 February 2026) announcing that, in its annual update of the cryptographic recommendations (TR-02102), the BSI for the first time sets end-of-life dates for classical asymmetric encryption (no sole use after end-2031, end-2030 for highly sensitive applications; classical signatures by end-2035), to be replaced by hybrid post-quantum cryptography. BSI President Plattner states the transition to post-quantum cryptography is 'alternativlos' (without alternative).

title: BSI erweitert kryptographische Empfehlungen mit Blick auf Quantencomputer
summary: BSI press release (10 March 2025) announcing an update to the TR-02102 technical guideline that extends the cryptographic recommendations to address the quantum-computer threat, recommending post-quantum algorithms (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, FrodoKEM, Classic McEliece, XMSS, LMS) and migration of high-security applications by 2030 in coordination with 17 European partners.

title: Sicheres Cloud-Computing: BSI veröffentlicht C5:2026
summary: BSI press release of 7 April 2026 announcing publication of the C5:2026 cloud computing criteria catalogue, stating that post-quantum cryptography and confidential computing are addressed explicitly in the new generation of C5 for the first time. Marks the point at which PQC enters Germany's cloud attestation regime.

title: C5:2026 Criteria Catalogue (Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue)
summary: The C5:2026 criteria catalogue itself, the successor to C5:2020, expanded from 121 to 168 criteria across 17 topic areas including cryptography and key management, and dedicatedly addressing post-quantum cryptography for the first time. Published in English and in a machine-readable format.

title: #nis2know: Kryptografische Verfahren – Konzepte und Prozesse
summary: BSI information package for NIS-2 regulated entities on cryptographic procedures, instructing them to take account of the migration to post-quantum cryptography and to trial first pilot environments in line with BSI recommendations. References the 2021 guide 'Kryptografie quantensicher gestalten', the August 2024 joint statement and the June 2025 EU roadmap.

title: Risiken im Fokus 2026 – Trend 1: Digitalisierung (Quantum Computing: Post Quantum Cryptography rückt in den Fokus)
summary: BaFin's 2026 risks-in-focus publication contains a dedicated post-quantum cryptography section stating that financial-sector firms must already act to identify quantum-endangered data and draw up a protection concept with a concrete implementation timeframe applying post-quantum cryptography, given the harvest-now-decrypt-later threat. BaFin also states it will set out supervisory expectations on quantum computing to regulated entities in 2026.

title: Post-Quanten-Kryptografie: BSI veröffentlicht Handlungsempfehlungen
summary: BSI news item of 26 March 2020 announcing an eight-page set of recommendations for action on migrating to post-quantum cryptography, stating that post-quantum cryptography will become the long-term standard and that organisations should assess the transition within their risk management, particularly for long-lived protected information.

title: Migration to Post Quantum Cryptography – Recommendations for action by the BSI
summary: BSI recommendations for action (dated 24 August 2020) on the transition to post-quantum cryptographic mechanisms. The foundational BSI PQC migration document that the later 2021 guide and the TR-02102 recommendations build on.

title: Kryptografie quantensicher gestalten – Grundlagen, Entwicklungen, Empfehlungen
summary: BSI guide published in December 2021 that updates and extends the 2020 PQC migration recommendations, summarising the state of research on quantum-safe cryptography, the connections between recent developments, current measures and open research questions. Still cited as the reference guide in BSI's NIS-2 material.

title: Bundestag printed paper 21/3915: Federal Government answer on the Hightech Agenda, covering the national post-quantum cryptography roadmap
summary: Federal Government answer to a Kleine Anfrage (Drucksache 21/3433, Die Linke) on the Hightech Agenda, stating that the EU roadmap requires member states to produce a first national roadmap for the transition to post-quantum cryptography by the end of 2026 and that a corresponding German document is being prepared within the Federal Government, to be published once complete.

title: Bundestag printed paper 21/5183: Kleine Anfrage on the reorientation of cybersecurity research
summary: Bundestag printed paper of 2 April 2026 asking how the Federal Government will align the priorities of new cybersecurity research funding with the existing framework programme, in which artificial intelligence and quantum technologies such as post-quantum cryptography were already emphasised.

title: Bundestag printed paper 21/765: Kleine Anfrage on the quantum-computer threat to encryption
summary: Kleine Anfrage of 7 July 2025 referring to the Federal Government's stated goal of presenting a strategy for the migration to post-quantum cryptography in Germany by 2026, and to the quantum-computer threat to encryption including cryptocurrencies. Answered in Drucksache 21/928, where BSI classifies the quantum threat as a very serious risk.

title: Hightech Agenda Deutschland – Quantentechnologien (technology roadmap dossier)
summary: BMFTR dossier page for the quantum technologies strand of the Hightech Agenda Deutschland, whose roadmap was presented in May 2026. States that quantum-safe encryption ('quantensichere Verschlüsselung') increases trust in information, communication and identification technologies, and frames the goal of future-proof cybersecurity in the quantum age.

title: Project Leap proves the viability of a quantum-safe financial system
summary: Deutsche Bundesbank press release on Project Leap, run with the BIS Innovation Hub Eurosystem Centre and Banque de France, in which test payment messages were transmitted through a quantum-resistant VPN tunnel between servers in Paris and Frankfurt to demonstrate protection of critical financial data using post-quantum cryptography.

title: Quantensichere Kryptografie: Bundesdruckerei entwickelt Prototypen einer Vertrauensinfrastruktur für Einsatz in Behörden
summary: Press release from the federally owned Bundesdruckerei on a prototype quantum-computer-safe public key infrastructure in test operation for use by public authorities, with the BSI supporting the selection of the cryptographic mechanisms and a hybrid classical/quantum-safe PKI envisaged for the transition phase. State-owned company rather than a government or standards domain, flagged for review.

title: Post-Quanten-Kryptografie: G7 Cyber Expert Group veröffentlicht Fahrplan
summary: BaFin notice of 14 January 2026 reporting that the G7 Cyber Expert Group, with BaFin participating, published a roadmap to promote the transition to post-quantum cryptography in the financial sector. It says the financial industry must now move to quantum-safe methods and that the non-binding approach foresees migration of critical systems by 2030.

title: Aktueller Umsetzungsstand des Handlungskonzeptes Quantentechnologien der Bundesregierung (Antwort der Bundesregierung, Drucksache 20/14986)
summary: Federal Government answer of 14 February 2025 (Bundestag printed paper 20/14986) to a CDU/CSU Kleine Anfrage on the implementation status of the quantum technologies action plan. In its joint answer to questions 62-66 it says that, working on the hypothesis that cryptographically relevant quantum computers will be available in the early 2030s, the government has initiated the transition to post-quantum cryptography in the high-security area. It notes a BSI-initiated paper in which security authorities from 18 EU member states call for prioritising PQC migration and protecting the most sensitive applications by end-2030. It says the government is involved in drafting an EU roadmap for the coordinated PQC transition, with the Interior Ministry and BSI co-leading the NIS Cooperation Group workstream alongside France and the Netherlands. It also mentions BSI quantum-safe recommendations since 2020 and approved classified-use devices with quantum-safe key exchange, and Annex 10 lists funded PQC projects.

title: Market Survey on Cryptography and Quantum Computing
summary: Joint survey by the BSI and KPMG Germany of organisations on their awareness of the quantum threat and the status of their migration to quantum-safe cryptography. It finds that few participants expect to become quantum-safe in good time and refers organisations to the BSI's quantum-safe cryptography recommendations.

title: Studie "Entwicklungsstand Quantencomputer" aktualisiert
summary: BSI news item of 19 December 2025 announcing an update of its study on the development status of quantum computers. Citing the store-now-decrypt-later risk, the BSI urgently recommends switching to quantum-safe cryptography.

title: Risiken für die Cybersicherheit durch Quantentechnologien
summary: Bundestag hib press note of 30 August 2023 summarising the Federal Government answer in Drucksache 20/8104 on cybersecurity risks from quantum technologies. It reports the government's aim to produce a strategy for migration to post-quantum cryptography in Germany by 2026 and the BSI's early PQC migration recommendations.
